blockingIssues.description: `test-node-run` and dependent scripts run without a compile prerequisite while migrated modules now depend on generated JS artifacts in `lib/`; in a clean checkout this can break node test workflows unless compile runs first.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Document the `allowJs` + emit incompatibility in mixed JS/TS in-place migrations and require explicitly removing or overriding `allowJs` when enabling emit.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Review of infra-setup-and-pilot reported this as an execution gotcha and the current skill guidance does not mention the caveat.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Clarify whether `.factory/**` operational artifacts should be committed as part of implementation feature commits versus treated as mission-local scaffolding.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The reviewed feature commit included multiple `.factory/**` files, but mission guidance focuses source migration scope and does not explicitly define commit boundaries for `.factory/**` artifacts.

rejectedObservations.observation: Worker used `bash .factory/init.sh` but `.factory/services.yaml` does not include an equivalent command.
rejectedObservations.reason: ambiguous ownership; bootstrap/init behavior may be mission-runner specific rather than a shared service command requirement

orchestratorOverride.reason: Scrutiny validator failed on round 2 because `npm run test-node` (full suite) includes integration tests with 4 pre-existing failures caused by Node.js v25.8.0 incompatibilities (posixExitCodes SIGABRT timeout and root-hooks ESM detection mismatch). These failures reproduce identically on the pre-migration commit (fb6bfd64) and are completely unrelated to the TypeScript migration. The blocking issue from round 1 (test-compile-gate) was fixed by feature fix-test-compile-gate. Unit tests, typecheck, lint, and build all pass cleanly. Overriding to allow mission progress.
